---
title: Sources & Tools
---

A source is a retrieval adapter. A tool is a model-visible action. Keeping them
separate lets the same corpus support search, visit, or a custom interaction
without putting model-facing schemas into the storage layer.

### Source contract

Every `DataSource` provides asynchronous `search`, `fetch`, and `close`
operations. Sources return provider-neutral `Document` and `SearchResult`
objects.

| `type` | Backend |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | Full-text search and file reads under a local root; requires `rg` |
| `web` | Serper search and Jina page fetching |
| `elasticsearch` | BM25, vector, or hybrid retrieval |
| `custom` | A project-defined `DataSource` class |

Each source needs a unique name. Source-backed tools refer to these names:

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: file
      name: project_docs
      root_path: ./docs
  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search_docs
      source: [project_docs]
    - type: visit
      name: visit_doc
      source: [project_docs]
```

### Elasticsearch retrieval

Elasticsearch supports `bm25`, `vector`, and `hybrid` search modes. Vector and
hybrid search require an embedding endpoint and a populated vector field.

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: elasticsearch
      name: corpus
      hosts: [http://127.0.0.1:9200]
      index: documents
      search_fields: [title, text]
      title_field: title
      text_field: text
      url_field: url
      vector_search_mode: hybrid
      vector_field: text_vector
      embedding_model: Qwen3-Embedding-8B
      embedding_base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8004/v1
      embedding_api_key: EMPTY
      embedding_prefix: |-
        Instruct: Given a web search query, retrieve relevant passages that answer the query
        Query:
      es_max_concurrency: 256
      embedding_max_concurrency: 256
```

### Agent tools

The tool name, description, and `inputSchema` are visible to the model. The
schema should expose only arguments the model can use correctly.

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search_web
      description: Search the indexed web corpus for relevant evidence.
      source: [corpus]
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        properties:
          keywords:
            type: string
            description: A focused search query.
        required: [keywords]
        additionalProperties: false
      argument_mapping:
        keywords: query
      raise_argument_validation_error: false
```

`argument_mapping` translates model-visible names to implementation arguments.

Set `raise_argument_validation_error: true` for training or RL workflows when
the upstream RL engine should receive an exception and penalize invalid calls. For
runs / evaluation, `false` would return the validation as a tool result to guide the agent to correct its request.

### Built-in tools

SearcherKit registers `search`, `visit`, and `mcp`.

#### `search`: retrieve candidate documents

`search` runs retrieval against a configured source. Its usual arguments are
`query` and `top_k`; `query` may also be a list, in which case queries are run
concurrently. Results contain titles, identifiers, links, and snippets. The
result metadata can include `searched_ids`, which is useful for recall analysis.

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search_docs
      source: [project_docs]
      response_char_limit: 20000
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        properties:
          query: {type: string, description: A focused search query.}
          top_k: {type: integer, minimum: 1}
        required: [query]
        additionalProperties: false
```

#### `visit`: fetch complete documents

`visit` fetches a document by `document_id` after `search` has identified a
candidate. `document_id` may be a list for concurrent fetches, and `goal` can be
passed to a configured summarizer.

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: visit
      name: visit_doc
      source: [project_docs]
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        properties:
          document_id: {type: string}
          goal: {type: string}
        required: [document_id]
        additionalProperties: false
```

#### `mcp`: call a remote tool

`mcp` adapts one remote MCP tool. `streamable-http` and `sse` transports are
supported. If `inputSchema` is omitted, it is discovered from the MCP server.

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: mcp
      name: remote_search
      endpoint: https://mcp.example.com/mcp
      transport: streamable-http
      mcp_tool_name: search
      auth_header: "Bearer ${MCP_TOKEN}"
      max_concurrency: 16
```

`search` and `visit` support `response_char_limit`. Results above the limit are
hard-truncated and marked `[Truncated]`; truncation is not summarization.

### Summerizer

Large search or visit results can be passed through a summarizer model so the agent could get the key information, and save context window. Summerizer requires an Openai Competable API, which requires the model to return:

```json
{"evidence": "Evidence realted to goal", "summary": "Concise summary"}
```

The result would be formatted and return as tool result string. Original tool extention field would be left unchanged.

Full config example:

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: visit
      name: visit
      source: [corpus]
      summary_goal_key: goal
      summarizer:
        model: Qwen3-8B
        base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1
        api_key: EMPTY
        max_chars: 40000
        max_concurrency: 128
        default_kwargs:
          max_tokens: 1024
        retry_config:
          max_tries: 3
```

`max_chars` limits the length of the raw content sent to the summarizer model;
it affects only the summarization request and does not change the tool's own
`response_char_limit`. `max_concurrency` uses a semaphore to limit the number
of summarization requests running at the same time. `default_kwargs` are merged
unchanged into the chat-completion request, for example `temperature` or
`max_tokens`. `summary_goal_key` specifies which tool argument supplies the
summarization goal: `search` usually uses `query`, while `visit` usually uses
`goal`. When `argument_mapping` is configured, use the mapped implementation
parameter name.
